units.source_text: 他以前不知道有这样的蜘蛛。

en.t: He had not known before that such spiders existed.

units.source_text: 用油灯代替巢，倒是挺时髦的。

en.t: Using an oil lamp instead of a web was rather stylish.

units.source_text: 巢里边只能被动地等待，使用油灯，就可以积极地把对方吸引过来。

en.t: Inside a web, it could only wait passively; by using an oil lamp, it could actively draw its prey toward it.

units.source_text: 只是这个方法必须有个前提，首先要让人准备适当的灯火。

en.t: But this method had one necessary condition: first, someone had to prepare a suitable light.

units.source_text: 很遗憾，大自然里是不可能有这种灯的。

en.t: Unfortunately, no such lamp could possibly exist in nature.

units.source_text: 它也决不会绕着月亮，绕着山林火灾闲逛的。

en.t: Nor would it ever go wandering around the moon, or around a forest fire in the mountains.

units.source_text: 难道这种蜘蛛是在人出现以后进化，把这习惯进化成本能的一个新种类吗？

en.t: Could this kind of spider be a new species that evolved after humans appeared, turning this habit into instinct?
... As an explanation, it was not half bad ...

units.source_text: 但是，这样的话，飞蛾的趋光性又打算如何来解释呢？

en.t: But if that was so, how did one intend to explain the phototaxis of moths?

units.source_text: ……和蜘蛛不同，你不能认为油灯对它们种类的保存能起到了什么作用。

en.t: ... Unlike with the spider, one could not suppose that oil lamps had played any role in preserving their species.

units.source_text: 而且，“趋光性”现象大约是灯火出现以后才有的，它们在这一点上完全相同。

en.t: Moreover, the phenomenon of phototaxis probably appeared only after lamps did, and in that respect they were exactly the same.

units.source_text: 小蛾子不会成群结队飞到月亮的世界里去，这就是最好的证据。

en.t: The best proof was that little moths did not fly off in swarms to the world of the moon.

units.source_text: 假如这只是其中一个种类的话，也许还能说得过去。

en.t: If this were true of only one species among them, perhaps it might still be explained.

units.source_text: 可是，这是约一万种左右的飞蛾共通的习性，看来这必然是俨然整肃的一个法则。

en.t: But this was a habit common to roughly ten thousand species of moths, so it seemed it must be a solemn and orderly law.

units.source_text: 它们被人工的油灯所引诱，这样盲目地、狂热地煽动着翅膀……

en.t: They were lured by man-made oil lamps, beating their wings so blindly and feverishly ...

units.source_text: 火、虫和蜘蛛，无缘无故地串通一气……

en.t: Fire, insects, and spiders, all conspiring together for no reason at all ...

units.source_text: 法则竟如此鲁莽地表现，究竟让人相信什么才好呢？

en.t: When law revealed itself in such a reckless way, what on earth was one supposed to believe?
